spatial_grounder on frame_57.50.png localizes the shared junctions at the left circle-diamond contact point bbox [185, 485, 225, 515] (confidence 0.98), the top corner [475, 325, 525, 355] (0.99), the bottom corner [475, 645, 525, 675] (0.99), the right corner [775, 485, 815, 515] (0.99), and a center point where the horizontal line intersects [475, 485, 525, 515] (0.99); frame_58.00.png gives the same five locations, including a center intersection bbox [475, 485, 525, 520] (0.98). So the grounded structure has five visible junctions: left contact, top, bottom, center intersection/left diamond vertex, and right corner.

Counting only the incidences explicitly grounded by chart_analyzer plus that center intersection from spatial_grounder: the left contact joins the two curved arcs and the horizontal segment, so its degree is 3; the top corner joins the upper curved arc and the two diamond sides meeting there, so degree 3; the bottom corner likewise has degree 3; the center intersection/left diamond vertex joins the horizontal segment and the two diamond sides, so degree 3; and the right corner is where the two diamond sides meet, so degree 2. That gives four odd-degree points.

By the Euler-path rule, a shape can be traced in one stroke only if it has exactly 0 or 2 odd-degree vertices. Here the tool-grounded junction count gives 4 odd vertices, so the last shape cannot be traced completely without lifting the pen or retracing. Answer: A.
